summary: Balax brings real infrared observations from NASA’s SPHEREx mission into a web viewer for the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. Visitors can compare two dates for the same patch of sky, inspect a difference map, and open the original FITS files. The public demo includes two verified fields, WISE 0855 and R Draconis. Showing the dates, wavelength band, and sources alongside the images helps students and citizen scientists document apparent changes and return to the underlying observations for follow-up.
details:
Balax makes repeat observations of the sky accessible in a web browser. We checked archive coverage for all five challenge targets using NASA/IPAC IRSA’s SIA2 service and the SPHEREx DR1 and QR3 collections. For the prepared pairs, we selected observations with overlapping wavelengths, aligned both images on a common sky grid using their FITS coordinates, masked unreliable pixels, and used the same brightness scale. We calculated the difference map by subtracting the earlier observation from the later one on pixels valid in both images.

Visitors can compare dates side by side, blink between them, or use a slider. They can inspect a difference map, open the original FITS files, and save an annotated report with its sources. Noise and instrumental effects can also create visible differences, so the comparison helps document features for follow-up.

We built the processing pipeline in Python with Astropy, NumPy, Reproject, and Pillow. FastAPI serves the results, and the web app uses JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Vite, and Three.js. Docker packages the application. The public demo serves verified, prepared DR1 pairs for WISE 0855 and R Draconis with live archive search disabled.

https://balax.me/#visor/wise-0855
https://balax.me/#visor?ra=248.167611&dec=66.754979

OpenAI Codex assisted with project planning, research, data analysis, software development, testing, and documentation. We used Google Stitch for early interface prototypes. Anthropic Claude assisted with the 3D map and the Web Audio code that synthesizes sound effects in the browser. ChatGPT helped prepare the slide deck. The astronomical observations come from NASA/IPAC IRSA’s SPHEREx archive. Balax derives its comparison images and difference maps from the original FITS files.
